claims.text: The CSV export file starts with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF), causing csv.DictReader to read the header key as '﻿region' instead of 'region', raising KeyError: 'region'
The fix changes report.py's open() call from encoding='utf-8' to encoding='utf-8-sig', which strips a leading BOM and is a no-op otherwise
A regression test test_utf8_bom_header_is_stripped was added using a new tests/data/bom.csv fixture, fails on old code and passes on new code
Full pytest suite passes (3 passed) and the CLI run of report.py produces correct output with exit code 0 after the fix
The response left the checked-in export file's BOM untouched, assuming the script should tolerate BOM-prefixed exports going forward
The transcript shows the model did not emit a debug brief before editing source; it opened with 'Fixed. Root cause: ...'
Grading for this run: 4 of 5 expectations passed (pass_rate 0.8), with the single failure being the missing debug-brief-before-editing expectation
The run used 12 total tool calls (5 Bash, 2 Read, 2 Edit, 3 Write) and encountered 0 errors
The run consumed 31480 total tokens and took 66.1 total duration seconds

A new eval, eval-2 'red-tests-after-merge', is defined with prompt about fixing 2 test failures in tests/test_pricing.py after a merge, including expectations about a debug brief, unchanged assertions, integer-cents/half-up rounding fix, and explaining binary float rounding
